extracted.intended_audience: Scholars, independent researchers, and writers preparing NEH Public Scholar Program book grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing an application to the NEH Public Scholar Program to fund a well‑researched humanities book aimed at a broad/general readership. Includes eligibility, project suitability, and presentation expectations for proposal materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for well‑researched books aimed at broad readership
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Scholar Program supports well‑researched books in the humanities intended to reach a broad readership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable projects present narrative history, tell stories of important individuals, analyze significant texts, synthesize ideas, revive interest in neglected subjects, or examine current thinking. The emphasis is on scholarship that can engage general audiences rather than narrowly specialized academic monographs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounding in humanities research and scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: Books supported by this program must be grounded in humanities research and scholarship, making appropriate use of primary and/or secondary sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate sound scholarly foundations and appropriate use of archival, primary, and secondary materials to support interpretation and argumentation; methodological rigor and citation of sources are implied expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readable, accessible prose for general readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects must be written in a readily accessible style, addressing significant humanities themes in a way that will appeal to a large audience of general readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity, engaging narrative or expository style, and avoidance of overly technical or disciplinary jargon are expected. The writing should translate scholarly knowledge for non‑specialists while maintaining scholarly integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate project type: works directed primarily to scholars
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to write books directed primarily to scholars are not appropriate for this program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the proposed book’s primary intended audience is specialists or it is highly disciplinary in form and content (e.g., an academic monograph with dense technical apparatus), it will not fit the program’s purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of acceptable subject approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Such scholarship might present a narrative history, tell the stories of important individuals, analyze significant texts, provide a synthesis of ideas, revive interest in a neglected subject, or examine the latest thinking on a topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these models as illustrations of approaches that translate humanities scholarship for broad audiences. Proposals should clarify which approach they adopt and why it will attract general readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility (affiliation and independent scholars)
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is open to both individuals affiliated with scholarly institutions and to independent scholars, researchers, and writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both institutionally affiliated and unaffiliated applicants may apply. The guidelines and application forms should be followed regardless of affiliation; institutional support letters or other documentation may be relevant where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project development stage (any stage allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects may be at any stage of development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are acceptable whether the project is in early planning, mid‑research, or near completion, but the application should clearly state the current stage, workplan, and how the grant will advance completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative/application requirements (deadlines and start dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt Deadline: February 6, 2019 for Projects Beginning September 2019. Updated guidelines will be posted at least two months in advance of the deadline listed above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must observe published deadlines and project start dates; check for updated guidelines in advance. Failure to meet submission deadlines or follow the most recent guidelines may render an application ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: DUNS number and Grants.gov/administrative prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: DUNS Number Requirement (and related Grants.gov registration resources listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet standard federal/grants administrative requirements such as obtaining any required DUNS/UEI numbers and registering with Grants.gov. The page points applicants to Grants.gov application packages, registration instructions, applicant tools, and PDF tools for preparing submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of provided resources and sample narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are directed to download application materials, sample application narratives, and program FAQs and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult sample application narratives and recently funded project lists to model proposal organization and level of detail. Use NEH‑provided templates and Grants.gov instructions to format and submit complete applications.
